html:
Bacalhau is dried and salted cod, the national food of Portugal. Portuguese like to say there is a recipe for each day of the year.

From the early 1500s Portuguese fishermen sailed to the Grand Banks off Newfoundland for cod, salting it on board. Salt cod kept well, could feed sailors on long voyages and suited the many Catholic fast days. Portugal also imported much of it from Norway and Iceland, kin to Norway's own stockfish.

Under Salazar the state backed a fleet of sailing ships, the White Fleet, that fished on the Grand Banks until the 1970s. Today Portugal still eats more cod than almost any nation, mostly from Norway. Bacalhau is the dish of Christmas Eve, as it is in parts of Spain and Brazil. See also the Cod Wars.
sum: Bacalhau is dried and salted cod, the national food of Portugal. Portuguese like to say there is a recipe for each day of the year.
